headers.comment: Vite fingerprints every file in /assets with a content hash, so a given URL's bytes can never change. Cache them permanently: on a repeat visit — or a flaky connection that reloads — nothing here is re-fetched.

Artwork is unhashed (served straight from /public) so it can't be immutable, but a day of browser cache plus a month of stale-while-revalidate means a returning visitor on bad internet paints instantly and refreshes in the background.
The HTML shell must always revalidate, otherwise a deploy that changes the asset hashes would never reach anyone holding a cached index.
